I farm 19.1 mu, wheat then maize, same as always. My land around Quzhou is fine silt, good for both crops. One person in my household, so I hire a combine at harvest and a rotary tiller between seasons — I cannot do it all myself at 64.

For winter wheat I plant around October 10. I use an improved variety, Jimai 22 or something similar — the seed dealer in town sells it, and my neighbors get around 500 kg/mu with it. I buy 15 kg seed per mu. Before planting I spread 50 kg of compound fertilizer (15-15-15) per mu as base — that is 7.5 kg N, 7.5 P, 7.5 K. Then at jointing in March I topdress 15 kg urea per mu, which is about another 7 kg N. Total nitrogen near 14-15 kg/mu. I know some people push 18-20 but I think that is wasteful on my soil, and urea prices have not been cheap. I irrigate at sowing, at jointing, and at grain-filling — three times from the well. Pesticide: one herbicide in spring, one spray for aphids and powdery mildew around April, sometimes a second if the aphids are bad. Call it two sprays. Rotary tillage before sowing, not deep plough — I only plough every three or four years.

For summer maize after wheat harvest in June, I direct-seed into the stubble, no-till, using a hybrid like Zhengdan 958 or Xianyu 335. 3 kg seed per mu. At sowing I put down 40 kg of 28-6-8 compound per mu in the row — that's about 11 kg N, 2.5 P, 3 K. At the big trumpet stage in late July I side-dress 15 kg urea, another 7 kg N. Total N around 18 kg/mu. Maize is hungrier than wheat. I irrigate once or twice depending on the rains — usually at tasseling if July is dry. Two pesticide sprays: one for armyworm and corn borer, one late for leaf disease if I see it. I expect 600 kg/mu in a normal year.

I do not change much year to year. What worked last year works this year. Fertilizer and diesel cost real money and with only me in the household I watch every yuan.
